subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should Linux Quick Chat be permitted to fetch agent avatar images from arbitrary `http:` and `https:` URLs supplied by local agent identity/configuration?
rationale: The code change intentionally expands a Tauri webview CSP and turns configuration data into outbound image requests; whether remote avatars are a supported trusted-config capability, and whether insecure `http:` must be allowed, is a maintainer-owned privacy and security boundary.

options.title: Allow constrained remote avatars
options.body: Accept remote avatar support only with an explicit documented trust contract and a narrowed policy such as `https:`-only plus a local fallback for unsupported URLs.

options.title: Keep avatars local only
options.body: Retain `self` and `data:` image sources and render emoji/monogram fallbacks for remote avatar URLs in Linux Quick Chat.

options.title: Approve the broad policy
options.body: Allow both `http:` and `https:` remote images as an intentional local-config capability and document the resulting network-fetch behavior.

recommendation.title: Allow constrained remote avatars
recommendation.body: Accept remote avatar support only with an explicit documented trust contract and a narrowed policy such as `https:`-only plus a local fallback for unsupported URLs.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Linux Quick Chat surface and authored the current implementation, making them the clearest available routing candidate for the policy discussion.
